_comment: Ratchet baseline for scripts/check-migration-privileges.py. Violations present when the rule was adopted. This list may only SHRINK — never add to it. R1/R2/R3/R4 are fixed FORWARD with a NEW migration that REVOKEs or pins search_path; migrations are immutable once applied, so never edit history. R5 (duplicate version timestamps) was different: it could only be fixed by renaming the colliding files, which BUGS-75 did on 2026-07-27 — all 6 collisions are resolved and the R5 entries are gone. NOTE for anyone reading the previous version of this comment: it claimed a rename had to be paired with a per-environment reconcile of supabase_migrations.schema_migrations, or the migration would re-apply. That was WRONG and it blocked the fix for weeks. Those tables are keyed on APPLY-TIME timestamps generated by the apply_migration MCP tool, not on repo file versions — none of the six colliding versions appeared in dev, staging or prod (verified 2026-07-27), and no pipeline runs 'supabase db push' against a remote project (CLAUDE.md gotcha #9). No database write was required. R2 entries for the two renamed files were re-keyed to their new filenames; the rule keys on filename. The live backstop for privileges is scripts/check-db-invariants.py.
